quote: Submerged. (time faded in scan; ~0615 by pattern)
Surfaced. Proceeding up east coast of Formosa. Wind and sea picking up from NNE to force 5.
Assumed strikes were called off. Submerged to re-stow gear and get some rest.
Submerged. We were being plagued by several different types of Jap radar
Surfaced. Sea state 3; visibility poor to fair but improving.
Surfaced. Sea fairly calm weather clear.
Surfaced. Floating object appeared to be wreckage of a small boat.
Submerged. Main induction failed to show closed at 30 feet so surfaced immediately.
Surfaced. Wind and sea force 2 weather fairly clear.
Surfaced to guard air rescue schedule.
Submerged. Seas too heavy to hold constant periscope depth.
Surfaced on lifeguard station. Sky completely overcast with strong wind and rough seas.
Surfaced to guard air rescue schedule.
Surfaced. Barometer high but seas still state 5 to 6 from NNE with heavy overcast.
Surfaced. Weather clear and seas moderating.
Completed search of probable southern sector. Dove and headed north
Dove for SJ contact at 4000 yds moving in fast nothing in sight.

As periscope was being swung in low power sweep QM saw plane on our port bow distance estimated 1½ miles in the act of letting a bomb go. Plane believed to be Val. Heard bomb through hull and a minute later another as we went to 150 feet.
Returned to periscope depth. All clear.
Sighted six single engine planes distance three miles zero angle flying low. Went deep. These boys are really earnest. (depth not stated)
Returned to periscope depth. All clear.
Surfaced. In view of stepped up air activity in this vicinity during the past several days and the full moon decided to move southwestward toward the Formosa coast.
Surfaced. Using SD intermittently since it is just beginning to get dark and a heavy overcast prevails.
SD contact closed to 4 miles. Dove.
Surfaced. Low barometer with force two wind and seas from south. ... Frequent squalls and lighting. St. Elmo's fire on radio antennas
Submerged. Had to keep sea on the beam to maintain periscope depth.
Experienced deep rumbling and heavy throbbing sensation lasting about 20 seconds. ... I am certain that this was an earthquake.
